source_text:
Ὅτι τὸ ἴσον μοι μὴ διδοὺς γνώμῃ τὸ πλέον παρέχεις ἄκων, καὶ ὃν δοκεῖς ἐπὶ ἀσθενείᾳ διασύρειν, ἰσχυρότε ρον τοῦ πατρὸς ἀποφαίνῃ· ὅτι ἐγὼ μὲν καὶ <μὴ>
παρακληθεὶς τὰς ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ κατεχομένας ψυχὰς ἐρρυσάμην· Κύριε, γάρ φησιν, ἀνήγαγες ἐξ ᾅδου τὴν ψυχήν μου, αὐτὸς δὲ καὶ παρακληθεὶς τὴν τεταραγμένην μου ψυχὴν τῶν ἐπηρτημένων οὐκ ἠλευθέρωσεν κακῶν. Ἀλλὰ μὴ γένοιτο! Οὔτε γὰρ ὁ 6 πατὴρ ἢ ἀφειδῶν ἢ ἀδυναμῶν οὐκ ἠλευθέρωσέν με τοῦ πάθους, οὔτε ἐγὼ παραιτού μενος τὸ πάθος ᾔτησα παρελθεῖν τὸ ποτήριον. Εἰ μὲν γὰρ ἀκού σιον τὸ πάθος, ἀληθῶς ἐδειλίων, εἰ δὲ αὐθαίρετος ὁ θάνατος, ἔδοξα δειλιᾶν, ἵνα σοφισάμενος τὸν διάβολον ἐλευθερώσω τὸν ἄνθρωπον. Ὅθεν τοῦτο μὴ συνορῶν ὁ διάβολος εἵλκυσέν με ὡς καταπίνειν μέλλων, ἀγνοῶν ὅτι καὶ τοὺς καταποθέντας ἐμέσαι εἶχεν. Ἅμα γὰρ ἐπέστην τῷ ᾅδῃ, ἐσκύλευσα αὐτοῦ τοὺς τάφους, ἐγύμνωσα τὰς θήκας. Ἐγύμνωσα δὲ οὐ φανερῶς μαχόμενος, ἀλλ' ἀοράτως τὴν ἀνάστασιν παρεχόμενος. Οὐδένα γὰρ ἔλυον καὶ πάντες ἀνίεντο, οὐδὲν ἐλάλουν καὶ ἐλευθερία ἐκηρύττετο, οὐδένα ἐκάλουν καὶ πάντες συνέτρεχον. Ἅμα γὰρ ἐπέστην ὡς βασιλεύς, κατεφρονήθη ὁ τύραννος, ἔλαμψα ὡς φῶς καὶ διελύθη τὸ σκότος. Ἦν γὰρ ἰδεῖν πάντα μὲν δεσμώτην ἐλευθερίαν βλέποντα, πάντα δὲ αἰχμάλωτον ἀναστάσει χορεύοντα· οὕτως ὡς αὐτοὺς τοὺς νεκροὺς ἐμὲ μὲν θαυμάζοντας ἐπὶ τῇ νίκῃ, τὸν δὲ θάνατον διασύροντας ἐπὶ τῇ ἥττῃ καὶ λέγειν· Ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον, ποῦ σου, ᾅδη, τὸ νῖκος; Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν οὕτως. Ὑπὲρ δὲ τῶν εἰρημένων δόξαν ἀναπέμψωμεν τῷ παμβασιλεῖ τῶν ὅλων Χριστῷ, ὅτι αὐτῷ πρέπει δόξα, τιμὴ καὶ προσκύνησις σὺν τῷ ἀχράντῳ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ παναγίῳ πνεύματι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν. 7
thought_title: Christ's voluntary death as deception of the devil
orientation: Christ is still speaking in the first person, answering the heretics' charge that his fear proves the Father's powerlessness.
pass_a_gloss: Because not giving me equality in judgment you grant the greater thing unwillingly, and the one whom you think to disparage for weakness you show to be stronger than the Father; because I, even without being called upon, rescued the souls held in Hades; 'Lord,' for it says, 'you brought up my soul from Hades,' but he, even when called upon, did not free my troubled soul from the impending evils. But may it not be! For neither did the Father, either being unsparing or being powerless, not free me from the passion, nor did I, refusing the passion, ask that the cup pass by. For if the passion were involuntary, truly I was afraid, but if the death is self-chosen, I seemed to fear, in order that having deceived the devil I might free the human being. Wherefore the devil, not seeing this, dragged me as if about to swallow me, not knowing that he would have to vomit up also those who had been swallowed. For at once I stood over Hades, I stripped his tombs, I laid bare the coffins. And I stripped them not by fighting openly, but by invisibly providing the resurrection. For I was releasing no one and all were being released, I was saying nothing and freedom was being proclaimed, I was calling no one and all were running together. For at once I stood over them as king, the tyrant was despised, I shone as light and the darkness was dissolved. For it was possible to see every prisoner seeing freedom, and every captive dancing in resurrection; so that the dead themselves were marveling at me for the victory, and disparaging death for the defeat, and saying: Where, death, is your sting, where, Hades, is your victory? And these things are so. And for the things that have been said let us send up glory to the king of all, Christ, because to him is fitting glory, honor, and worship with the undefiled Father and the all-holy Spirit unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.term: τὸ ἴσον μοι μὴ διδοὺς γνώμῃ τὸ πλέον παρέχεις ἄκων
choices.english: not giving me equality in judgment you grant the greater thing unwillingly
choices.why: Keeps the paradox of the heretics' position: by denying equality they inadvertently grant superiority. 'Judgment' for γνώμῃ preserves the sense of considered opinion or verdict.
rejected: not giving me equal honor in your opinion you grant more against your will
by not granting me equality in your view you unwillingly grant the greater

choices.why: διασύρειν means to tear apart or ridicule; 'disparage' captures the mocking tone of the heretics' charge.
ἀφειδέω means to be unsparing or not to spare; the participle suggests the Father withholding mercy, which the text denies.
σοφίζομαι in patristic Greek often means to outwit or deceive by cleverness; 'deceived' matches the glossary's 'deception' theme.
σκυλεύω means to strip a fallen enemy of arms or spoil; 'stripped' conveys the plundering of death's domain.
ἀοράτως means invisibly; παρεχόμενος means providing or furnishing. The contrast is with open battle.

pass_b_english: By not granting me equality willingly, you grant me the greater thing against your will. The one you think you are disparaging for weakness, you are actually declaring stronger than the Father. For I, without even being urged on, rescued the souls held down in Hades. “Lord,” it says, “you brought up my soul from Hades” (Psalm 30:3). But he, even when urged on, did not free my troubled soul from the evils hanging over it. But let it not be so! For neither was the Father sparing or powerless when he did not free me from the passion, nor did I, in refusing the passion, ask for the cup to pass by. If the passion were involuntary, then I truly feared. But if the death was self-chosen, then I only appeared to fear, so that by deceiving the devil I might set humanity free. The devil did not see this, and so he dragged me down, intending to swallow me, not knowing that he would have to vomit up even those he had already swallowed. For the moment I stood in Hades, I stripped his tombs and laid bare his graves. I laid them bare not by fighting openly, but by invisibly providing the resurrection. I was releasing no one, and yet all were being released. I was saying nothing, and yet freedom was being proclaimed. I was calling no one, and yet all were running together. For the moment I stood there as king, the tyrant was despised. I shone as light, and the darkness was dissolved. You could see every prisoner looking at freedom, every captive dancing at the resurrection—so much so that the dead themselves were marveling at me for the victory and mocking death for its defeat, saying: “Where, death, is your sting? Where, Hades, is your victory?” (Hosea 13:14). And so it is. For all that has been said, let us send up glory to Christ, the king of all, for to him belong glory, honor, and worship, with the undefiled Father and the all-holy Spirit, to the ages of ages. Amen.
